ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.claim: The Prophet should patiently receive and convey revelation rather than rush to recite it; God guarantees its collection, preservation, explanation, and elucidation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.anchor: The Almighty is revealing it as per His wisdom and expediency.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r1.claim: The pronoun in ‘in your chest’ refers to the Qur’an, and qurʾan here means its recitation; the cited poem also uses qurʾanan for reciting.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r2.claim: Another explanation takes qurʾan as the Qur’an’s composition and collection in the Prophet’s chest, from the root meaning to collect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r2.anchor: وقيل: وقرآنه: وتأليفه في صدرك، فهو مصدر من قرأت: أي جمعت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God preserves the Qur’an during the Prophet’s life and arranges its recitation on his tongue.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r8.anchor: وفي التحرير والتحبير قال ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says God establishes the Qur’an in the Prophet’s heart after collecting it for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك: نثبته في قلبك بعد جمعه لك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r10.claim: Another report explains its collection as Gabriel repeating the revelation to the Prophet until it settles in his chest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r10.anchor: وقيل: جمعه بإعادة جبريل عليك مرة أخرى إلى أن يثبت في صدرك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the Prophet hurried both to memorize and ask about meaning; the command assures preservation and defers questions until recitation ends.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.anchor: ثم إن علينا بيانه: إذا أشكل عليك شيء من معانيه، كأنه كان يعجل في الحفظ

NAHHAS:v5p81/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p81/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p81/r10.claim: God guarantees collection of the Qur'an, refuting claims that any part remained unrevealed.
NAHHAS:v5p81/r10.anchor: فيضمن الله جل وعز جمعه فبهذا كفر الفقهاء من زعم أنه قد بقي منه شيء

NAHHAS:v5p81/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p81/r11.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
NAHHAS:v5p81/r11.claim: Sufyan explains that God entrusted Torah and Gospel preservation to their people, but kept the Qur'an in His own care, as 5:44 and 15:9 show.
NAHHAS:v5p81/r11.anchor: وسئل سفيان بن عيينة كيف غيرت التوراة والإنجيل وهما من عند الله فقال أن الله جل وعز وكل حفظهما إليهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.claim: The surah describes gathering on Judgment Day in gathering bones and sun with moon, and earthly gathering in collecting and reciting the Quran.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.anchor: وذكرت نوعين من الجمع، جمعاً في يوم القيامة وجمعاً في الدنيا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.claim: God is described with plural forms such as We are able, We gather, and We shape, as well as singular forms such as He created and proportioned.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.claim: If the address were to humanity generally, the pronouns could refer to a person’s inward knowledge: do not rush to voice it, since God gathers and recites it and one should follow.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.anchor: hesab başında Hakk’ın huzûrunda vicdânındakini acele söyleyip de işin içinden çıkacağım diye telaş etme

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.claim: The pronoun’s antecedent is not explicit; a universal-human addressee could make it refer to what is within a person, namely conscience.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.anchor: Bu âyetteki بِهِۦ zamirlerinin merci‘i zâhir değildir. Hitab mutlak insana olsaydı

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.claim: Because the address is specifically to the Prophet and the passage later names the Qur’an, the pronouns first refer to the Qur’an being revealed; an implied antecedent is sufficient, as at 97:1.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.anchor: hitab bilhassa Peygamber’e olmak ve sonra da “Kur’an” denilmiş bulunmak itibariyle bu بِهِۦ zamirinin evvelâ

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.claim: The exegetes identify the pronouns as referring to the Qur’an.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.anchor: Onun için tefsirler bu بِهِۦ zamirlerinin Kur’ân’a râci‘olduğunu beyan etmektedirler.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r14.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r14.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet moved his lips while Qur’an was descending so he could memorize it, and this verse was revealed in response.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r14.anchor: Tirmizî de bunun sebeb-i nüzûlünü Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr, İbn Abbas’tan şöyle rivayet eylemiştir

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.claim: The Prophet should listen while revelation arrives rather than hurry to recite; God undertakes gathering and reciting it, then he follows Gabriel’s completed reading.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.anchor: sade dinle, acele okumak için dilini oynatma

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.claim: Here “Qur’an” is a verbal noun meaning recitation, though it may also mean the recited text.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.claim: The revelation discussion is integrated with the preceding account of conscience rather than left as a digression, joining the beginning and end of the passage.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.anchor: bu âyetleri bu sûrede bir istitrad hâlinde bırakmayarak evvelini âhirine tamamen yapıştırmıştır.

RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r4.claim: The Prophet’s excuse was fear of forgetting; because preservation comes through God’s aid, he should stop hastening and rely on divine guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r4.anchor: فههنا كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم يظهر التعجيل في القراءة مع جبريل ، وكان يجعل العذر فيه خوف النسيان

RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r6.claim: As an unbeliever flees from God toward others, Muhammad should turn from reliance on repetition to God; the parallel command in Ṭā Hā asks him to seek knowledge from God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r6.anchor: كن كالمضاد له فيجب أن تفر من غير الله إلى الله وأن تستعين في كل الأمور بالله

RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl proposes that the address concerns a person shown his record at resurrection: God reads and gathers his deeds, commands confession, then explains his punishment; this is a strong warning though unsupported by reports.
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.anchor: قال القفال : فهذا وجه حسن ليس في العقل ما يدفعه وإن كانت الآثار غير واردة به

RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r1.claim: The particle ʿalā conveys obligation, so “upon Us” signals that preservation is incumbent upon God in the sense explained by the competing theological schools.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r1.anchor: كلمة على للوجوب فقوله : إن علينا

RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī’s school holds that God’s obligation to preserve the revelation follows from His promise.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r2.anchor: أما على مذهبنا فذلك الوجوب بحكم الوعد

RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r3.claim: The Muʿtazilites say preservation is required by divine wisdom, since the purpose of prophethood cannot be fulfilled unless revelation is protected from forgetfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r3.anchor: وأما على قول المعتزلة : فلأن المقصود من البعثة لا يتم إلا إذا كان الوحي محفوظا مبرأ عن النسيان

RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r4.claim: “Its gathering” means collecting the revelation in the Prophet’s breast and preserving it there.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r4.anchor: قوله : { إن علينا جمعه } معناه علينا جمعه في صدرك وحفظك

RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r5.claim: If Qurʾānah means recitation, Gabriel may repeat the revelation to Muhammad until he memorizes it.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r5.anchor: أن يكون المراد جبريل عليه السلام ، سيعيده عليك حتى تحفظه

RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r6.claim: Alternatively, God may recite it to Muhammad until he no longer forgets, as promised in al-Aʿlā.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r6.anchor: إنا سنقرئك يا محمد إلى أن تصير بحيث لا تنساه

RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r7.claim: Qurʾān may mean collection or composition; Arabic usage applies the root to a camel gathering a fetus and to a woman not having gathered one.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r7.anchor: أن يكون المراد من القرآن الجمع والتأليف

RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r8.claim: If both terms mean gathering, the first is the revelation’s external existence and the second its mental preservation and memorization, avoiding redundancy.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198/r8.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد من الجمع جمعه في نفسه ووجوده الخارجي ، ومن القرآن جمعه في ذهنه وحفظه

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r1.claim: The verses tell the Prophet to wait patiently for revelation to continue, paralleling the instruction in 20:114.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r1.anchor: These verses address the Prophet, encouraging him to wait patiently for the continuation of the revelation

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r2.claim: The verses refer to the Prophet’s fear of forgetting revelation, which made him repeat quickly what had come even while revelation continued.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r2.anchor: Both passages are understood as references to the Prophet’s fear of forgetting the verses of revelation, which led him to repeat quickly everything that had been revealed to him

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r3.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet bore revelation with difficulty and moved his lips quickly; God promised to make him remember the revealed portion by heart and recite it.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r3.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said, “The Messenger of God used to bear the

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r7.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r7.claim: God gathers the Quran in the Prophet’s breast so he remembers it correctly.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r7.anchor: God will gather it within the Prophet’s breast, ensuring that he remembers it correctly

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r8.claim: The passage can admonish Quran students to read and reflect on all its teachings before drawing hasty conclusions.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r8.anchor: These verses can also be taken as an admonition to those who wish to understand the Quran to first read and reflect upon all of its teachings

TAB-FULL:v23p496#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p496#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p496#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet hurried to recite and memorize each revelation, moving his lips; God told him not to hasten and promised to gather and recite it for him.
TAB-FULL:v23p496#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا نزل عليه القرآن تعجل يريد حفظه

TAB-FULL:v23p499/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p499/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p499/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Muhammad continually reviewed the Qur’an for fear of forgetting; God would gather and teach it to him so he would not forget.
TAB-FULL:v23p499/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به}

TAB-FULL:v23p500/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p500/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p500/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Saʿīd ibn Jubayr’s report from Ibn ʿAbbās: the prohibition concerns hurrying before the Qur’an is gathered; review for memory would occur after God gathered it.
TAB-FULL:v23p500/r3.anchor: وأشبه القولين بما دل عليه ظاهر التنزيل

TAB-FULL:v23p501/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r1.claim: God undertakes to gather the Qur’an in Muhammad’s chest and establish it there, then enable him to recite it.
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، {إن علينا جمعه} [القيامة: 17] قال: في صدرك

TAB-FULL:v23p501/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains gathering as placing it in Muhammad’s chest and its Qur’an as his reciting it afterward.
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، {إن علينا جمعه}

TAB-FULL:v23p501/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God gathers the Qur’an for Muhammad and teaches him to recite it so he will not forget.
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه}

TAB-FULL:v23p501/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God gathers the Qur’an for Muhammad and establishes it in his heart.
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه} [القيامة: 17] يقول

TAB-FULL:v23p501/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r5.claim: Qatāda interprets the phrase as preserving the Qur’an and composing or arranging it.
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه}

TAB-FULL:v23p501/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r6.claim: Qatāda takes qurʾānah as composition, deriving it from a verb for a she-camel enclosing a fetus; ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm’s line uses لم تقرأ جنينا for that sense.
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r6.anchor: وكأن قتادة وجه معنى القرآن إلى أنه مصدر

TAB-FULL:v23p501/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take qurʾānah as the verbal noun of reciting or reading: قرأت أقرأ قرآنا وقراءة.
TAB-FULL:v23p501/r7.anchor: وأما ابن عباس والضحاك فإنما وجها ذلك إلى أنه مصدر

TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report says God undertakes to make the Prophet recite without forgetting; when it is recited to him, he should follow its contents.
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.anchor: عن أبيه، عن عبد الله بن عباس

TAB-FULL:v1p92/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r1.claim: The poetic phrase لم تقرأ جنينا means she did not enclose a womb with a child, illustrating qaraʾa as gathering or containing.
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r1.anchor: يعني بقوله: لم تقرأ جنينا: لم تضمم رحما على ولد

TAB-FULL:v1p92/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r2.claim: Qatādah interprets God’s gathering and recitation of the Qur’an as its preservation and arrangement.

TAB-FULL:v1p92/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes قرآنه to mean God’s clarification through His recitation: once it is explained to the Prophet, he must follow that explanation.
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r4.anchor: صح ما قال ابن عباس في تأويل قوله

TAB-FULL:v1p92/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r5.claim: Both Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation and Qatādah’s composition sense are valid Arabic, but each revealed verse bound the Prophet before the Qur’an was compiled.
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r5.anchor: ولكلا القولين أعني قول ابن عباس وقول قتادة، اللذين حكيناهما، وجه صحيح في كلام العرب

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.claim: These four verses interrupt the resurrection description with divine etiquette for the Prophet receiving revelation: listen until recitation is complete. Their instruction resembles 20:114.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.anchor: الآيات الأربع في معنى قوله تعالى ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r4.claim: Qur’an is a verbal noun like furqan and rajhan; its pronouns refer to revelation, which God gathers in parts and recites without omission.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r4.anchor: القرآن ها هنا مصدر كالفرقان والرجحان

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r5.claim: A reported interpretation says God gathers the Qur’an in the Prophet’s heart so its meanings do not escape him and establishes its recitation on his tongue; the author considers this remote.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r5.anchor: وقيل المعنى إن علينا أن نجمعه في صدرك بحيث لا يذهب عليك شيء من معانيه

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.claim: Some say the Prophet moved his tongue during revelation for fear of forgetting and was told to listen until it ended; the pronoun means what had already been recited to him.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم في معنى هذه الآيات إن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يحرك لسانه عند الوحي بما ألقي إليه من القرآن مخافة أن ينساه

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r2.claim: The fear-of-forgetting account does not fit: the verses more plainly prohibit haste and command following God’s completed recitation, while gathering and recitation supports the author’s reading.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r2.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائم سياق الآيات، تلك الملاءمة نظرا إلى ما فيها من النهي عن العجل والأمر باتباع قرآنه تعالى بعد ما قرئ

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.claim: Another interpreter says these verses concern a person reading his record on Judgment Day, not the Qur’an: God gathers the evidence, demands submission, then explains it if denied.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.anchor: وعن بعضهم في معنى هذه الآيات، الذي اختاره أنه لم يرد القرآن

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.claim: The record-reading view fails because an interrupting passage needs no contextual signs before and after it, and its resemblance to 20:114 supports the Qur’anic reading.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.anchor: ويدفعه أن المعترضة لا تحتاج في تمام معناها إلى دلالة مما قبلها وما بعدها عليه

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.claim: A further view connects the verses to Judgment: do not hasten to ask when it will come; God gathers those destined for it, reveals its description, and clarifies it by the trumpet blast.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.anchor: وعن بعضهم أن الآيات الأربع متصلة بما تقدم من حديث يوم القيامة، وخطاب { لا تحرك } للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.claim: The Judgment-day reading is untenable to the author.

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that revelation weighed on the Prophet, who moved his lips to memorize; God promised to gather and recite it, told him to listen, and promised its explanation; thereafter he listened to Gabriel and recited after he left.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة، وكان يحرك به

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes similar reports from Ibn Jubayr and others, but says the fit between this explanation and the verses is obscure.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.anchor: روى ما في معنى صدر الحديث في المجمع عن ابن جبير وفي معناه غير واحد من الروايات، وقد

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r7.claim: God promises to gather the Quran securely in the Prophet’s breast, so no meaning escapes; this also means establishing recitation on his tongue for later use.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r7.anchor: في صدرك بحكم الوعد بحيث لا يخفى عليك شيء من معانيه

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r8.claim: Qurʾān here is a verbal noun meaning recitation, like ghufrān for forgiveness; it means joining letters and words in ordered recitation, not any gathering.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r8.anchor: فالقرآن مصدر بمعنى القراءة كالغفران بمعنى المغفرة

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r12.speaker: الواسطي
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r12.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads gathering the Quran as inward and recitation as outward.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r12.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله جمعه في السر وقرآنه في العلانية

TABRISI:75:16/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:16/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:16/r6.claim: Qurʾān derives from gathering and joining and is a verbal noun like rajḥān and nuqṣān.
TABRISI:75:16/r6.anchor: والقرآن أصله الضم والجمع وهو مصدر كالرجحان والنقصان

TABRISI:75:17-24/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:75:17-24/r2.claim: Qatāda says God will gather the revelation in the Prophet's breast so he memorizes it, and arrange its recitation in the revealed order.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r2.anchor: { إن علينا جمعه } في صدرك حتى تحفظه { وقرآنه } أي وتأليفه على ما نزل عليك عن قتادة

TABRISI:75:17-24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
TABRISI:75:17-24/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say God gathers and recites it to the Prophet so he can memorize and recite it without fear of losing any part.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه عليك حتى تحفظه ويمكنك تلاوته فلا تخف فوت شيء منه

TABRISI:75:17-24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r8.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:75:17-24/r8.claim: On al-Balkhī's reading, the servant rushes through his record in distress at seeing sins; God tells him to wait while the evidence is gathered and then submit to the judgment and its consequences, unable to deny it.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r8.anchor: فإنا نجمعها لك فإذا جمعناه فاتبع ما جمع عليك بالانقياد لحكمه والاستسلام للتبعة فيه فإنه لا يمكنك إنكاره

THALABI:v10p86#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p86#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p86#2/r10.claim: God undertakes to gather the revelation in the Prophet's chest so that he memorizes it.
THALABI:v10p86#2/r10.anchor: إن علينا جمعه في صدرك حتى تحفظه

THALABI:v10p86#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p86#2/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p86#2/r11.claim: “Its recitation” means God will recite it to the Prophet so he understands it.

THALABI:v10p86#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p86#2/r12.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p86#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, “its recitation” means gathering it in the Prophet's chest; the noun is a verbal form like rajḥān and nuqṣān.
THALABI:v10p86#2/r12.anchor: وقيل أراد بقوله: وقرآنه وجمعه في صدرك وهو مصدر كالرجحان والنقصان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says God will gather the Qur’an in the Prophet’s breast and recite it to him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r5.claim: Ata interprets the promise as Gabriel repeating the revelation to the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء: (أي) (¬4) إن جبريل يستعيده عليك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r6.claim: Muqatil says this means, “We will recite it to you” until you have memorized it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل (وقرآنه): يعني: ونقرئكه حتى تحفظه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God will make the Prophet recite it so he does not forget, as in 87:6; on this reading the Prophet recites it, while on the preceding reading Gabriel does.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: إن علينا أن نقرئكه فلا تنسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل، مجاهد، قتادة، عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r8.claim: Muqatil, Mujahid, Qatada, and Ata share this explanation of the command not to move the tongue during revelation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r9.claim: Qatada glosses gathering and reciting as preservation; Qur’an connects to gathering, as in the expression that a she-camel had not gathered a fetus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r9.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله: (جمعه وقرآنه) حفظه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r10.claim: Qur’an can mean gathering, as in the expression that a she-camel had not collected a fetus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p496#2/r10.anchor: ما قرأت الناقة سلا (¬2) قط، أي: ما جمعت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r2.claim: The omitted referent of “it” is the revelation, understood from context, as the omitted referent in 97:1 is understood despite being the sura’s opening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r2.anchor: ليس المراد بقوله: {جمعه وقرآنه} القرآن الذي هو اسم التنزيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r3.claim: The pronoun in the verbal noun refers to the revelation as its object, so it means “our gathering it and our reciting it,” not that the named Qur’an is added to itself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r3.anchor: وإذا كان الذكر المضاف إليه المصدر في قوله: (وقرآنه) راجعا إلى التنزيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda takes the phrase figuratively as collecting and arranging the parts; the camel expression and Amr ibn Kulthum’s line use qaraʾa for gathering or carrying a fetus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r5.anchor: مجاز الآية على قول أبي عبيدة: جمعه وتأليف بعضه إلى بعض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r6.claim: Pairing general gathering with the more specific Qur’an or recitation is apt repetition, like gathering people or wealth, where one would not say “read the people.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r6.anchor: وإنما حسن ذكر الجمع والقرآن؛ لأن المجى عام، والقرآن أخص منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r7.claim: A second term adding a meaning absent from the first is especially apt, as when “inform” is paired with “warn.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r7.anchor: كما أنك لو قلت: أعلمت زيدا وأنذرته، حسن؛ لاختصاص الإنذار بمعنى التخويف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r1.claim: God undertakes to gather and recite the Qur’an to the Prophet so he understands it.

QASHANI:75:17-19/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:75:17-19/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:75:17-19/r1.claim: God gathers the Quran within the addressee at the station of unity, reciting it through him while he is effaced from self and has no remaining existence or trace.
QASHANI:75:17-19/r1.anchor: جمعه فيك وقرآنه أي: ليكن جمعه في مقام الوحدة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r2.claim: God undertook to gather the revelation in memory and writing and ensure that the Messenger would not forget it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r2.anchor: Vahyi hafızalarda ve yazılı olarak toplayıp Resûlullah’ın unutmamasını sağlamak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r3.claim: God also undertook to enable the Prophet to recite the revelation.

BURHAN:v2p126/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p126/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p126/r4.claim: The author invokes God's promise to preserve the Reminder and collect and recite the Qur'an against claims of additions, omissions, or textual alteration.
BURHAN:v2p126/r4.anchor: وبذلك يسقط اعتراض الملحدين فى القرآن وذلك دليل على صحة نقل القرآن وحفظه وصيانته من التغيير

BURHAN:v2p126/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p126/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p126/r5.claim: The community agrees that preservation means guarding the Qur'an for practice and from error or confusion, which warrants certainty in the communal codex.
BURHAN:v2p126/r5.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة أن المراد بذلك حفظه على المكلفين للعمل به وحراسته من وجوه الغلط والتخليط

BURHAN:v1p278/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p278/r5.claim: God gathers the Quran in the Prophet's heart as memorization, on his tongue as recitation, and in his hearing as understanding and knowledge.
BURHAN:v1p278/r5.anchor: أى جمعه فى قلبك حفظا وعلى لسانك تلاوة وفى سمعك فهما وعلما

BURHAN:v1p278/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p278/r6.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
BURHAN:v1p278/r6.claim: Some of the author's colleagues say the listener hears a created recitation while understanding through it God's eternal speech.
BURHAN:v1p278/r6.anchor: قال بعض أصحابنا إن عند قراءة القارىء تسمع قراءته المخلوقة ويفهم منها كلام الله القديم

BURHAN:v1p233/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p233/r1.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
BURHAN:v1p233/r1.claim: Al-Bukhari reports that after heavy losses among Quran reciters at Yamama, Umar warned Abu Bakr that more deaths could cause Quranic material to be lost and urged its collection; Abu Bakr hesitated because the Prophet had not done so, but Umar persuaded him.
BURHAN:v1p233/r1.anchor: روى البخارى فى صحيحه عن زيد بن ثابت قال أرسل إلى أبو بكر مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر بن الخطاب عنده

BURHAN:v1p233/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p233/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
BURHAN:v1p233/r2.claim: Abu Bakr chose Zayd, a young, trusted writer of revelation, to gather the Quran; after initial hesitation, Zayd collected it from writing materials and people's memories.
BURHAN:v1p233/r2.anchor: إنك رجل شاب عاقل لا أتهمك وقد كنت تكتب الوحى لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فتتبع القرآن واجمعه قال زيد فوالله لوكلفنى نقل جبل

BURHAN:v1p233/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p233/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p233/r6.claim: The four Companions known as Quran preservers were renowned examples, not the only memorizers; the whole Quran was memorized and arranged during the Prophet's life, apart from the cited exception of Bara'a.
BURHAN:v1p233/r6.anchor: والمراد أن هؤلاء كانوا اشتهروا به فقد ثبت أن غيرهم حفظه وثبت أن القرآن مجموعة محفوظ كله صدور الرجال أيام حياة النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURHAN:v1p48/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p48/r2.claim: Because the unlettered Prophet moved his tongue as revelation came, he was told to reflect rather than hurry to repeat it; God would gather and preserve it.
BURHAN:v1p48/r2.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أميا لا يقرأ ولا يكتب وكان إذا نزل عليه الوحى وسمع القرآن حرك لسانه

BURHAN:v1p388#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p388#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p388#2/r1.claim: The written alif marks a word considered through concrete, lower, or knowable reality; its omission marks a metaphysical, attributive, or higher aspect beyond sense.
BURHAN:v1p388#2/r1.anchor: فإن الألف تحذف فى الخط علامة لذلك واعتبار من جهة ملكية حقيقية فى العلم أو أمور سفلية فإن الألف تثبت

BURHAN:v1p388#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p388#2/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p388#2/r2.claim: The Qur'an details verses established in the comprehensive Book, so it is nearer to understanding and clearer in revelation; its alif is written, while كتاب omits it.
BURHAN:v1p388#2/r2.anchor: فالقرآن أدنى إلينا فى الفهم من الكتاب وأظهر فى التنزيل

SULAMI:v2p361#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r1.claim: God gathers the Quran within the secret and recites it aloud in public.
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : جمعه في السر وقراءته في العلانية

SULAMI:v2p361#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r2.claim: The Quran was deposited in the innermost secrets and its explanation in the inward hearts.
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي : جمعه في السر وقراءته في العلانية . وقال : أودع القرآن سرائرهم واودع البيان بواطنهم

SULAMI:v2p361#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r3.claim: The Prophet was told not to rely on himself in any matter: God would care for all his affairs, gather the Quran in his breast, and make its recitation easy on his tongue.
SULAMI:v2p361#4/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : قيل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : لا تستعن بنفسك على شيء من اسبابك فإنا لا نكلك

KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.claim: They object that 75:16–19 interrupts the flow from the preceding passage about a person's self-witness to the warning about preferring worldly life, and say each topic should occupy its own section.
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.anchor: وقد يدخل بين الكلامين ماليس من جنسهما ولا قبيلهما كقوله سبحانه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r1.claim: Qarya names a large gathering of people and derives from gathering; qaraʾtu al-māʾ means collecting water in a basin.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r1.anchor: القرية : اسم لما يجمع جماعة كثيرة من الناس . وهو اسم مأخوذ من الجمع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r2.claim: The basin holding collected water is called a maqrāh.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r2.anchor: ويقال : للحوض الذي فيه الماء : مقراة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says qarʾ means gathering and Qur’an is so named because its speech is collected.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : والقرء في اللغة الجمع . وسمي القرآن قرآنا لأنه كلام مجتمع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the Qur’an is named for gathering and joining its sūras together.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r4.anchor: ( وقال ابن قتيبة : سمي القرآن قرآنا ) لأنه جمع السور وضمها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda’s poem illustrates qaraʾa for carrying or gathering a fetus.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r5.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة : - هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r6.claim: In 75:17, “its gathering and recitation” means its compilation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p499#2/r6.anchor: وقوله : ﴿ إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه ﴾ ، أي : تأليفه

FARRA:v3p211/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p211/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p211/r1.claim: The Quran's recitation is assured; Gabriel will repeat it to Muhammad so he can recite it.
FARRA:v3p211/r1.anchor: وقرآنه» وقراءته، أي: أن جبريل عليه السلام سيعيده عليك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#3/r1.claim: He glosses the gathering and Qur’an of revelation as its joining and collection.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#3/r1.anchor: {إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه} أي ضمه وجمعه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says Qur’an here means composition: the Qur’an is named for collecting and joining its sūras.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r2.anchor: وقال في قوله: {إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه} (6) أي تأليفه. قال: وإنما سمي قرآنا لأنه جمع السور وضمها.

MAJAZ:v1p17/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r1.claim: He explains jamʿahu wa-qurʾānahu as composition and fa-idhā qaraʾnāhu as collection, supporting this sense with Amr ibn Kulthum's use of qaraʾa for containing a fetus.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r1.anchor: «إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه» (75/ 17) : أي تأليفه «فإذا قرأناه» (75/ 18) أي إذا جمعناه

SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r1.claim: قرآنه means its recitation, a verbal noun annexed to its object with the agent omitted; the sense is وقراءتك إياه.
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r1.anchor: أي: قراءته، فهو مصدر مضاف للمفعول. وأما الفاعل فمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r2.speaker: حسان
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r2.claim: Ḥassān's verse uses قرآنا for recitation, describing a person passing the night in praise and recitation.
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r2.anchor:
قال حسان رضي الله عنه:
4415.....................
يقطع الليل تسبيحا وقرآنا

SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports Abū al-ʿĀliya's جمعه وقرانه and فاتبع قرانه; the author relates the reading to Ibn Kathīr's earlier variant discussion.
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r3.anchor: قال أبو العالية: " إن علينا جمعه وقرانه. فإذا قرته فاتبع قرانه

ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r5.claim: God undertakes to teach the Prophet the revelation so he will not forget it and to recite it to him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r5.anchor: أي إن عليناأن نقرئك فلا تنسى، وعلينا تلاوته عليك

ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r2.claim: God undertakes to gather the revelation in the Prophet's heart and cause it to be read as it ought.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r2.anchor: it is for Us to gather it

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.claim: The passage also applies to every believer who reads, listens to, or studies the Qur'an, and should be read with 20:114 and its note 101.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.anchor: both have also a wider import inasmuch as they apply to every believer who reads, listens to or studies the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.claim: While 20:114 warns against hasty conclusions from isolated verses, this passage calls for patient study of the whole message and careful attention to every word and phrase.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.anchor: not to draw hasty - and therefore potentially erroneous - conclusions from isolated verses or statements of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.claim: Readers and listeners should avoid mechanical fluency or delight in beautiful Qur'anic sound without understanding its message.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.anchor: remain satisfied with the mere beautiful sound of the Qur'anic language without understanding

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n7/r1.claim: Gathering the revelation means causing the Prophet to remember it and read with mind and heart; it must be understood as one integrated whole, not as disconnected maxims, stories, or laws.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n7/r1.anchor: make thee remember it and to cause it to be read with mind and heart

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p211/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p211/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p211/r6.claim: The Prophet would race Gabriel's recitation while receiving revelation, fearing it might slip from memory; he was told to listen with heart and hearing until Gabriel finished.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p211/r6.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا لقن الوحي، نازع جبريل القراءة، ولم يصبر إلى أنْ يُتِمَّها مسارعةً إلى الحِفْظِ وخوفاً من أن يتفلَّتَ منه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p212/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p212/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p212/r2.claim: Preposing ‘upon Us’ makes God's guarantee exclusive: only God can gather, preserve, and enable correct full recitation of the Qur'an; the meaning and verse ending require the order.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p212/r2.anchor: الملاحظ في هذا التعبير أنه قدم الجار والمجرور على الاسم، وذلك للاختصاص والقصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p212/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p212/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p212/r3.claim: Moving the prepositional phrase later would remove the exclusive guarantee and alter the meaning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p212/r3.anchor: ولو أخر الجار والمجرور لأخل بالمعنى، ذلك أنه يقتضي عدم القصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r1.claim: His comparison shows that ‘Khalid explains this to you’ is not exclusive, while fronting ‘to you’ implies that he explains it only to you; fronted prepositional phrases usually restrict.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r1.anchor: فإنك ذكرت أن خالداً يشرح له الأمر ولم تُفِدْ أن خالداً يخصه بالشرح لأحدٍ غيره

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r2.claim: Inna supplies the reason for the tongue command by linking it to God's guarantee; without it the clauses lose their causal connection, as illustrated by 9:103.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r2.anchor: من ذلك أنها تفيد التعليل كما في قوله تعالى: {وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ صلاوتك سَكَنٌ لَّهُمْ} [التوبة: 103]

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r3.claim: Inna also emphasizes the promise, since retaining and reproducing everything accurately from hearing alone is extraordinary.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك أنها تفيد التوكيد، وهذا الموطن يقتضي التوكيد إذ إن حفظ الإنسان لكل ما يُلْقى إليه بمجرد سماعه أمرٌ غريب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.claim: These verses tell the Prophet to be patient amid his opponents’ pressure and repeated demands, while he waits for revelation to answer them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.anchor: These verses urge the Prophet (sws) to be patient on the hast iness and various new

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.claim: Only revelation gave the Prophet the guidance needed to carry out his grave duty of publicly warning his people; he depended on his Lord at every step.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.anchor: He was like a soldier, fighting at a battle front, who could not move even one step without guidance from his Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.claim: They also objected that a Qur’an from God should have been revealed all at once, and used such challenges to obstruct the Prophet’s mission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.anchor: Similarly, they would object that if the Qur’ ān was God’s word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.claim: Revelation strengthened the Prophet’s heart and resolve, renewed his soul, and guided his intellect as he faced his opponents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.anchor: It was through divine revelation that his heart would receive strength, his soul would be rejuvenated, his intellect guided

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.claim: The Qur’an and Hadith indicate that during divinely wise pauses in revelation the Prophet looked toward heaven; when Gabriel recited, he was eager to learn and preserve every word.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.anchor: Consequently, it is evident both from the Qur’ ān and Ḥad īth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.claim: The Prophet needed revelation for the strategy of his mission as God’s Messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.anchor: All the strategy that needed to be adopted by him in the capac ity of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.claim: Revelation alone could meet his spiritual, moral, and intellectual needs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.anchor: His spiritual, moral and intellectual needs could only be fulfille d

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.claim: It supplied guidance for circumstances the Prophet faced and those still to come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.anchor: He would receive from it the guidance needed to face existing and future circumstances.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.claim: It enabled him to answer the objections and demands his adversaries continually raised.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.anchor: It was through it that he was able to answer the objections and demands which his adversaries would keep posing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.claim: His love of knowledge and care to preserve it also contributed to his eagerness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.anchor: His great love for knowledge and his sensitivity in preserving it also contributed very much to it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.claim: Though the Prophet’s motives were noble, divine wisdom required gradual revelation, so he was repeatedly urged to be patient.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.anchor: it was God’s wisdom that the Qur’ ān be revealed gradually

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.claim: The Prophet receives a similar exhortation to patience in Sūrah Ṭāhā.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.anchor: In S ūrah Ṭāhā (114-115) too he has been similarly urged.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.claim: Here the Prophet is also assured that God will preserve, collect, arrange, recite, and explain the Qur’an, so he can be content with what is revealed and leave its timing to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.anchor: here he has been subsequently assured of the preservation of the Qur’ ān also.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.claim: He should accept the portion revealed, avoid anxiety about its preservation, and trust that each task will be completed at its appointed time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.anchor: He was also not to worry about its preservation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r1.claim: The assurance answers the Prophet’s natural anxiety about safeguarding the great trust: preserving and reciting the Qur’an is God’s responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r1.anchor: The Almighty assured him that the responsibility of preserving and reciting it was His responsibility.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r2.claim: Jamʿ covers both preserving the Qur’an in the Prophet’s heart and assembling its separate parts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r2.anchor: a comprehensive one: it means preservation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r3.claim: God guided the placement of revealed verses within their sūrahs, and the Prophet instructed the collectors where to insert them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r3.anchor: he would direct the collectors to insert these verses at their specific places.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r4.claim: Narratives report that the Prophet recited the Qur’an revealed to date to Gabriel each Ramadan to guard against lapses of memory; in his final Ramadan they recited it twice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r4.anchor: various narratives that in the last Rama ḍān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.claim: Farāhī accepts the exegetes’ view that haste partly reflected fear of losing Qur’anic material, while adding that the Prophet saw himself entrusted with a grave responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.anchor: I do not differ with this view; however, there are some more details

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.claim: Farāhī says the Prophet feared accountability for losing even a letter, while also seeking more revelation to guide his people; the assurance addresses both concerns.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.anchor: he thought that he was being given a great responsibility

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r3.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r3.claim: Farāhī connects the assurance of preservation with Qur’anic declarations that falsehood cannot reach the Scripture.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r3.anchor: The preservation of the Qur’ ān has been promised by the Almighty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r4.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r4.claim: Farāhī cites God’s promise to preserve the Reminder as proof that no addition or deletion in the Qur’an is possible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r4.anchor: It was We Who revealed the Reminder

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r5.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r5.claim: He says the Muslim community agrees that the Qur’an has remained preserved, without additions or deletions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r5.anchor: there exists a consensus in the whole of this ummah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r6.speaker: Sayyid Murtaḍā, Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī, Abū ʿAlī Ṭabarī, Ṭabrasī, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh al-Qummī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r6.claim: The named Imāmī authorities reject the claim that part of the Qur’an disappeared; the source says the attributed popular view contradicts their positions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r6.anchor: Ab ū ‘Al ī Ṭabar ī, Ṭabras ī (the author of Majma‘ al-bay ān), Muhammad ibn ‘Al ī ibn B ābawayh al-Qumm ī – all have vehemently denied this absurd view.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r7.speaker: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh al-Qummī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r7.claim: Al-Qummī says the Qur’an found between the covers is precisely what God revealed to the Prophet, with no additional letter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r7.anchor: al-Qumm ī says: “It is our belief that the very

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r1.speaker: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Bābawayh al-Qummī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r1.claim: Al-Qummī continues that the Qur’an has no extra material and calls those who attribute belief in a longer Qur’an to the Imāmiyyah liars.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r1.anchor: the Qur’ ān more than this. A person who attributes to us the view

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r2.speaker: Sayyid Murtaḍā
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r2.claim: Murtaḍā says dissenters among the Imāmiyyah and Ḥashawiyyah rely on weak reports, which cannot overturn a proven and certain reality.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r2.anchor: a proven and certain reality cannot be rejected.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r3.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r3.claim: Farāhī concludes that collection, arrangement, and a recital sequence occurred during the Prophet’s lifetime, since he was told to follow the newly recited text.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r3.anchor: If this promise was to be fulfilled after his death, he would not have been aske d

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r4.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r4.claim: He infers that the Prophet communicated the final Qur’anic sequence as recited to him, matching the original sequence in the Guarded Tablet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r4.anchor: this directive means that the Prophet (sws) must have communicated the final arrangement of the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.claim: Farāhī says these conclusions follow from the Qur’an and Hadith: the Prophet recited whole sūrahs in sequence, and Companions memorized and followed that arrangement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.anchor: Consequently, the Prophet (sws) would read out whole sūrahs of the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.claim: He says the Prophet directed Companions to place each revealed verse in its assigned position within a particular sūrah, and they obeyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.anchor: direct the Companions (rta) to place the revealed verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r3.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r3.claim: Authentic, agreed-upon reports say that after the Qur’an was fully revealed Gabriel recited it to the Prophet in its true sequence, resolving doubts about its arrangement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r3.anchor: once the whole of the Qur’ ān had been revealed, Gabriel recited the complete Qur’ ān

QIRAAT-ER:75:17:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:75:17:5#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:75:17:5#1/r1.claim: Hamza easing reduces the pronounced hamza in wa-Qurānahu while preserving the same q-r-ʾ recitation field.
QIRAAT-ER:75:17:5#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Canonical hamza-lightened form reduces the pronounced hamza while preserving the same q-r-ʾ recitation field

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#4/r1.claim: Qatāda explains God's gathering and recitation of the Qurʾān as its preservation and compilation.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ جمعه وقرآنه ﴾ قال حفظه وتأليفه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r1.claim: God gathers the Qur’an in the Prophet’s breast so that none of its meanings escapes him.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r1.anchor: إن علينا جمعه في صدرك بحيث لا يذهب عليك شيء من معانيه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r2.claim: Qur’an here means recitation: God establishes its reading on the Prophet’s tongue so he can recite whenever he wishes.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r2.anchor: وقرآنه أي إثبات قراءته في لسانك بحيث تقرأه متى شئت فالقرآن هنا وكذا فيما بعد مصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r3.claim: As evidence that Qur’an means recitation, the commentary cites a poetic line in which قرآنا names nightlong reciting and glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r3.anchor: ضحوا باشمط عنوان السجود به يقطع الليل تسبيحا وقرآنا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r4.claim: On the recitation sense, قرآنه is a verbal noun annexed to its object, with an omitted annexed word understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r4.anchor: مضاف إلى المفعول وثم مضاف مقدر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r5.claim: Another explanation takes جمعه as preserving the Qur’an during the Prophet’s life and قرآنه as its composition or collection on his tongue; al-Alusi questions these accounts, though the first is attributed to Mujahid.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r5.anchor: وقيل قرآنه أي تأليفه والمعنى إن علينا جمعه أي حفظه في حياتك وتأليفه على لسانك وقيل قرآنه تأليفه وجمعه على أنه مصدر قرأت أي جمعت

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r6.claim: The alternate etymology relates qara’a to gathering, as in the idiom for a woman who has not conceived and the cited line of ‘Amr ibn Kulthum about a camel that has not conceived.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#2/r6.anchor: ومنه قولهم للمرأة التي لم تلد ما قرأت سلي قط وقول عمرو بن كلثوم ذراعي بكرة أدماء بكر هجان اللون لمتقرأ جنينا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.claim: God will gather the Quran in the Prophet's breast and enable its recitation; when Gabriel recites it, the Prophet should listen and follow, and God will explain it through his tongue.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.anchor: قال علينا أن نجمعه في صدرك، وقرآنه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas's account says the Prophet would bow his head when Gabriel came, then recite after he left; another transmission says he moved his lips for fear the revelation might escape.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r2.anchor: فكان إذا أتاه جبريل عليه السلام أطرق فإذا ذهب قرأه كما وعده الله عز وجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r3.claim: The transmission through Ibn Abbas explains the gathering as placing the Quran in the Prophet's breast and its quran as his reciting it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r3.anchor: عن موسى بن أبي عائشة بهذا الإسناد وقال: كان يحرك شفتيه إذا نزل عليه، يخشى أن ينفلت منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:14-17/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:14-17/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:14-17/r7.claim: God will gather the Qurʾān in the Prophet's chest and establish its recitation on his tongue; this explains the prohibition on haste.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:14-17/r7.anchor: وإثبات قراءته في لسانك وهو تعليل للنهي

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.claim: The passage reinforces the rebuke against haste: haste is blameworthy even in the most important matter and foundation of religion, and therefore all the more elsewhere; it may also recall an event during revelation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.anchor: وهو اعتراض بما يؤكد التوبيخ على حب العجلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.claim: Alternatively, the speech addresses the person receiving his record: he stumbles in fear as he hurries to read it, so God promises to gather and read his deeds; he should acknowledge or reflect on the reading, then God explains it through requital.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.anchor: وقيل الخطاب مع الإنسان المذكور والمعنى أنه يؤتى كتابه فيتلجلج لسانه من سرعة قراءته خوفا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r5.claim: Through Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibn ʿAbbās reports that revelation strained the Prophet, who moved his lips; God revealed these instructions, after which he listened silently to Gabriel and recited the passage when Gabriel left. No grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج

DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet moved his tongue and lips under revelation’s strain, fearing he would forget; the verses promise collection and recitation, attentive following, and clarification, after which he listened and recited when Gabriel left.
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة وكان يحرك به لسانه وشفتيه مخافة أن يتلفت منه

DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet persisted in reciting from fear of forgetting; God undertook to gather and recite it so he would not forget, commanded him to follow it, and to explain its lawful and unlawful rulings.
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يفتر عن القرآن مخافة أن ينساه فقال الله

DURR-FULL:v8p348/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p348/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p348/r2.claim: Qatadah says the Prophet moved his tongue for fear of forgetting; God’s undertaking means preserving and assembling the Qur’an.
DURR-FULL:v8p348/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به} قال: كان نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحرك لسانه بالقرآن مخافة النسيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r1.claim: In both places, قرآن is the verbal noun meaning recitation, like غفران and فرقان; Hassan ibn Thabit’s elegy for Uthman witnesses the usage قرآنا.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r1.anchor: و ( قرآن ) في الموضعين مصدر بمعنى القراءة مثل الغفران والفرقان ، قال حسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r2.claim: In both clauses, علينا expresses God’s undertaking and guarantee.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r2.anchor: ولفظ { علينا } في الموضعين للتكفل والتعهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r4.claim: God guarantees gathering revelation, its recitation, and—above that—its explanation by the Prophet, preserved in his heart and clear to hearers without consulting a written copy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r4.anchor: أن علينا جمع الوحي وأن تقرأه وفوق ذلك أن تبينه للناس بلسانك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas in Sahih al-Bukhari says revelation strained the Prophet, who moved his lips fearing loss; God guaranteed to gather it in his breast.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r4.anchor: وهو في صحيح البخاري عن ابن عباس: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r5.claim: قرآنه may mean the Quran's recitation, that Muhammad himself will perform; Quran is a verbal noun like qira'a, as in Hassan ibn Thabit's line about Uthman.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r5.anchor: وقرآنه يحتمل أن يريد به وقراءته أي تقرأه أنت يا محمد، والقرآن مصدر كالقراءة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r6.claim: Alternatively, قرآنه means collecting and arranging the revelation in Muhammad's breast, since قرأت can mean جمعْت; he cites usage for a woman who has not given birth and poetry by Amr ibn Kulthum.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد إن علينا جمعه وتأليفه في صدر صدرك فهو مصدر من قولك قرأت أي جمعت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#2/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#2/r1.claim: Gathering and reciting it means collecting it in the Prophet's breast.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي ضمه وجمعه في صدرك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.claim: God teaches the Prophet to listen rather than race the angel in receiving revelation, promising to collect it in his heart, enable its recitation, and explain it; these are its three stages.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.anchor: هذا تعليم من الله عز وجل لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كيفية تلقيه الوحي من الملك، فإنه كان يبادر إلى أخذه، ويسابق الملك في قراءته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r3.claim: God’s gathering of the Quran means preserving it in the Prophet’s chest.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r3.anchor: إن علينا جمعه} أي: في صدرك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r4.claim: “Its recitation” means that the Prophet will recite the Quran.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that revelation caused the Prophet strain and he moved his lips; God told him to listen while Gabriel recited, promised to gather the Quran in his chest, and afterward the Prophet recited it as taught.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة، فكان يحرك شفتيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.speaker: البخاري ومسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.claim: Bukhari and Muslim transmit the report by multiple routes; Bukhari’s wording says the Prophet lowered his head when Gabriel came, then recited after Gabriel left as God had promised.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.anchor: وقد رواه البخاري ومسلم، من غير وجه، عن موسى بن أبي عائشة، به (2) ولفظ البخاري: فكان إذا أتاه جبريل أطرق، فإذا ذهب قرأه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet read continuously for fear of forgetting; God promised to gather the Quran for him and recite it to him so that he would not forget.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به} قال: كان لا يفتر من القراءة مخافة أن ينساه

JISHUMI:v10p7183/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r17.claim: Qurʾān derives from gathering and joining and is a verbal noun like rujḥān and nuqṣān; qaraʾtu water in a basin means I gathered it.
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r17.anchor: والقرآن: أصله من الضم والجمع، وهو مصدر كالرجحان والنقصان

JISHUMI:v10p7184/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain God's gathering it as placing the Qurʾān in the Prophet's chest until he memorizes it, and its recitation as enabling him to repeat and explain it.
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r10.anchor: قيل: إن علينا جمعه في صدرك حتى تحفظه، وقرآنه عليك حتى تعيد

JISHUMI:v10p7184/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r11.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r11.claim: Qatādah explains gathering as collecting the Qurʾān in the Prophet's chest and arranging it in the order revealed to him.
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r11.anchor: إن علينا جمعه في صدرك، وتأليفه على ما نزل عليك، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7184/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r12.claim: Another view takes the promise as God's preserving the Qurʾān for the Prophet so he can recite it.
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r12.anchor: وقيل: علينا حفظه عليك لتصل إلى الأداء

JISHUMI:v10p7184/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r13.claim: The aim is not merely recitation and memorization but reflection on the Qurʾān and knowledge of its meanings and rulings; preservation is God's responsibility, so the Prophet should attend to his own duty.
JISHUMI:v10p7184/r13.anchor: فأشار إلى أن المقصود ليس مجرد التلاوة والحفظ؛ بل التدبر فيه

JISHUMI:v10p7186/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r11.claim: The phrase ʿalaynā signals obligation because ʿalā is a word of obligation; once commissioned, the Prophet was obliged to explain what removes the accountable person's excuse.
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r11.anchor: ويدل قوله: (إن علينا جمعه) أنه يجب عليه شيء؛ لأن (على) كلمة إيجاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r5.claim: God guarantees to collect the Qur'an in the Prophet's heart and establish its recitation on his tongue.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r5.anchor: في صدرك وإثبات قراءته في لسانك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God gathers the Quran in the Prophet's heart so he can recite it with his tongue.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r3.anchor: أحدها : إن علينا جمعه في قلبك لتقرأه بلسانك , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r4.claim: Qatada understands gathering and recitation as God's preservation and arrangement of the Quran.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r4.anchor: الثاني : عيلنا حفظه وتأليفه , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says God gathers the Quran for the Prophet until it is firmly retained in his heart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r5.anchor: الثالث : عيلنا أن نجمعه لك حتى تثبته في قلبك , قاله الضحاك .

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#8/r1.claim: God will gather the Qur'an in the Prophet's breast and establish its recitation on his tongue.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#8/r1.anchor: ﴿ إن علينا جمعه ﴾ في صدرك ﴿ وقرآنه ﴾ واثبات قراءته في لسانك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#8/r2.anchor: والقرآن القراءة ونحوه ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى اليك وحيه

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.claim: The Muslim and Bukhari account says the Prophet listened to Gabriel recite, then recited as taught; Ibn Abbas and Saʿid demonstrate the lip movement.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.anchor: عن ابن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r3.claim: God gathers the revelation in the Prophet’s breast and recites it to him; he is to listen and follow its recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r3.anchor: قال جمعه في صدرك ثم تقرؤه

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats qirāʾa and Qurʾān as verbal nouns; Qurʾānah here means recitation to the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r7.anchor: والقراءة والقرآن في قول الفراء مصدران
